title: IPv6 multicast and MLDv2 authority boundary
summary: RxSock6 dev3 does not advertise multicast membership. IPv6 multicast is supplied by IP Multicast v0.1-dev2 through the family-aware RFC 3678 provider path; MLDv2 remains host-stack behaviour below that socket interface.
invariants: Do not add an RxSock6-specific multicast semantic layer when the common IP Multicast RFC 3678 provider already owns membership.
IPv6 ASM/SSM/full-state filtering uses IPPROTO_IPV6 and native MCAST_* operations through IP Multicast dev2.
A host membership observation in /proc/net/igmp6 demonstrates the operating-system IPv6 membership route; it is not an ooRexx MLDv2 implementation.
PIM-SM remains routing/control-plane infrastructure and must not be surfaced as a fake application socket method.
procedure: When multicast is requested, keep the Inet6Address object intact and route membership through the common IP Multicast provider contract.
Describe MLDv2 evidence as host-stack behaviour unless packet-level MLD conformance is independently implemented and qualified.

provenance.claim: Records RxSock6 dev3 UDP6, IP Multicast dev2 IPv6 RFC 3678 ASM/SSM/filter qualification, live ff02::115 delivery, /proc/net/igmp6 membership observation, and the MLDv2/PIM-SM authority boundary.
provenance.note: IPv6 datagram and multicast evidence delta.
